claims.quote: Eosinophils typically represent 2–4 percent of total leukocyte count. They are also 10–12 µm in diameter.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads of chromatin
a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads of chromatin
The nucleus of the eosinophil will typically have two to three lobes

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: one or more slender chromatin threads joining the nuclear lobes
claims.quote: a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads of chromatin

claims.value: eosinophil granules; look: unknown; abundance: many; position: unknown
claims.quote: Granular leukocytes contain abundant granules within the cytoplasm. They include neutrophils, eosinophils, and basophils

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Its granules carry antihistamine molecules, so it can counter the histamine that basophils and mast cells release.
claims.quote: The granules of eosinophils include antihistamine molecules, which counteract the activities of histamines, inflammatory chemicals produced by basophils and mast cells.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Some of its granules hold molecules that are toxic to parasitic worms, which equips it against worm infections.
claims.quote: Some eosinophil granules contain molecules toxic to parasitic worms, which can enter the body through the integument, or when an individual consumes raw or undercooked fish or meat.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It can also engulf targets by phagocytosis, and does this best when antibodies have coated the target.
claims.quote: Eosinophils are also capable of phagocytosis and are particularly effective when antibodies bind to the target and form an antigen-antibody complex.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Called by T cell cytokines to where parasitic worms have settled in the gut, it releases the contents of its granules when it arrives.
claims.quote: some worms take up residence in the gastrointestinal tract. Eosinophils are attracted to the site by T cell cytokines, which release their granule contents upon their arrival.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It can latch onto a parasite that IgE antibody has labelled, binding it through an Fc receptor.
claims.quote: Furthermore, if IgE labels the parasite, the eosinophils can bind to it by its Fc receptor.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Like neutrophils, it engulfs large pathogens such as bacteria and fungi.
claims.quote: Neutrophils and eosinophils are particularly important leukocytes that engulf large pathogens, such as bacteria and fungi.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It produces extra inflammatory mediators that bring in more leukocytes.
claims.quote: Eosinophils and basophils produce additional inflammatory mediators to recruit more leukocytes.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

tier1.text: Any of the immature or mature forms of a granular leukocyte with a nucleus that usually has two lobes connected by one or more slender threads of chromatin, and cytoplasm containing coarse, round granules that are uniform in size and which can be stained by the dye eosin. Eosinophils are CD9-positive, CD191-positive, and CD193-positive.
tier1.attribution: Definition from the Cell Ontology (CL 2026-06-08), CL:0000771. CC BY 4.0.
